title: Revisiting Re-executability: Coverage-Guided Symbolic Feedback to Improve Decompilation
abstract: arXiv:2611.18892v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When source code is unavailable, decompilation provides a source-level representation of a binary. However, code recovered by conventional or LLM-assisted decompilation may not preserve the original behavior of the binary. Recent approaches evaluate re-executability using fixed test suites, but passing these suites does not ensure behavioral preservation. We present SymDec, an LLM-assisted decompiled-code repair system that uses the original binary as a behavioral reference. SymDec uses coverage-guided symbolic execution to explore the I/O-level behavior of the original and recompiled binaries, and symbolic comparison to identify inputs that expose behavioral differences. These inputs are replayed on both binaries to confirm the differences, which are returned as structured feedback to guide subsequent LLM revisions. We evaluate SymDec on 120 functions from ExeBench and DecompileBench, compiled for x86-64 and ARM64 at optimization levels

translated_title: 重新审视可重执行性：覆盖率引导的符号反馈以改进反编译
translated_abstract: 当源代码不可用时，反编译可以为二进制文件提供源代码级别的表示。然而，通过传统方法或大语言模型（LLM）辅助反编译恢复的代码可能无法保留原始二进制文件的行为。近期的方法使用固定测试套件来评估可重执行性，但通过这些测试套件并不能确保行为保真。我们提出了SymDec，一个以原始二进制文件作为行为参考的LLM辅助反编译代码修复系统。SymDec使用覆盖率引导的符号执行来探索原始二进制与重编译二进制在I/O层面的行为，并通过符号比较识别出暴露行为差异的输入。这些输入随后在两个二进制文件上重放以确认差异，并作为结构化反馈返回，用于指导后续的LLM代码修订。我们在来自ExeBench和DecompileBench的120个函数上评估了SymDec，这些函数针对x86-64和ARM64架构在不同优化级别下编译。
tldr: SymDec系统利用覆盖率引导的符号执行对比原始二进制与重编译二进制的I/O行为，将暴露行为差异的输入作为结构化反馈指导LLM修复反编译代码，从而超越固定测试套件、真正确保行为保真。
en_tdlr: SymDec employs coverage-guided symbolic execution to compare the I/O-level behavior of original and recompiled binaries, replaying inputs that expose behavioral differences as structured feedback to guide LLM-based repair of decompiled code, thereby ensuring true behavioral preservation beyond fixed test suites.
